body:
Closes #34258

## What I did
Replaces the duplicated `typeof framework === 'string' ? {} : framework.options.builder || {}` ternary across 6 framework preset files with the existing `getBuilderOptions` utility from `storybook/internal/common`.

## Checklist for Contributors

### Testing

#### The changes in this PR are covered in the following automated tests:
- [x] stories
- [x] unit tests
- [x] integration tests
- [x] end-to-end tests

#### Manual testing
This is a pure refactor with no behaviour changes. The existing `getBuilderOptions` utility is already tested. No manual testing required.

### Documentation
- [ ] Add or update documentation reflecting your changes
- [ ] If you are deprecating/removing a feature, make sure to update [MIGRATION.MD](https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/blob/next/MIGRATION.md)

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Refactor**
  * Consolidated builder-options resolution across Angular, Ember, Next.js Vite, React Webpack5, and Server Webpack5 into a single shared utility, replacing per-framework conditional logic.
  * Standardized behavior with no changes to public APIs or exported signatures; end-user behavior and configuration surface remain unchanged.

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

**`getBuilderOptions` changes semantics versus the previous inline expression.**

Line 43 now includes `core.builder.options` fallback (via `getBuilderOptions`), while the previous code only used `framework.options.builder || {}`. That is a behavior change, so this is not strictly a pure refactor. Please either preserve framework-only semantics here (and sibling presets) or explicitly update PR intent/tests to cover the new precedence.



<details>
<summary>Possible minimal fix to preserve previous behavior in this preset</summary>

```diff
 export const core: PresetProperty<'core'> = async (config, options) => {
   const framework = await options.presets.apply<StorybookConfig['framework']>('framework');
+  const frameworkBuilderOptions =
+    typeof framework === 'string' ? {} : framework.options.builder ?? {};
@@
     builder: {
       name: fileURLToPath(import.meta.resolve('@storybook/builder-webpack5')),
-      options: await getBuilderOptions(options),
+      options: frameworkBuilderOptions,
     },
```
</details>

<!-- suggestion_start -->

<details>
<summary>📝 Committable suggestion</summary>

> ‼️ **IMPORTANT**
> Carefully review the code before committing. Ensure that it accurately replaces the highlighted code, contains no missing lines, and has no issues with indentation. Thoroughly test & benchmark the code to ensure it meets the requirements.

```suggestion
export const core: PresetProperty<'core'> = async (config, options) => {
  const framework = await options.presets.apply<StorybookConfig['framework']>('framework');
  const frameworkBuilderOptions =
    typeof framework === 'string' ? {} : framework.options.builder ?? {};

  return {
    builder: {
      name: fileURLToPath(import.meta.resolve('@storybook/builder-webpack5')),
      options: frameworkBuilderOptions,
    },
  };
};
```

</details>

<!-- suggestion_end -->

**Use optional chaining to safely access the `options` property on line 6.**

Per the `Preset` type definition, `options` is optional (`options?: any`). When a framework preset does not include an `options` property, accessing `framework.options.builder` will throw a `TypeError`. This pattern is already used safely in the similar utility `get-builder-options.ts` and across multiple framework presets in the codebase.

<details>
<summary>🐛 Proposed fix using optional chaining</summary>

```diff
-  return typeof framework === 'string' ? {} : framework.options.builder || {};
+  return typeof framework === 'string' ? {} : framework.options?.builder ?? {};
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```

return expression in get-framework-builder-options (the ternary using variable
framework) can throw when a Preset lacks options — change the access to use
optional chaining so we safely read builder: for non-string framework values,
use framework.options?.builder || {} instead of framework.options.builder,
ensuring the function returns an empty object when options or builder are
missing.
```

</details>
